definitions.meaning: a single round of ammunition fired from a gun
a musket ball, the old name for a lead shot

explanation.surface: A single round ball, perhaps in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A round of ammunition and a musket ball are both a single shot for a gun.

parts.note: black means dirty, as with grime
to eye is to look at, and an eye is a look

explanation.surface: A mouse gives someone a filthy glare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouse' is slang for a bruised eye, not the rodent; 'Dirty look' wants to be the definition but supplies the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouse is slang for a bruise round the eye after a punch.

clue.text: Evil is cut out of Book Three

indicators.note: out means the letters of the words before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: Wickedness has been removed from the third volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EVILISCUT; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The third book of the Old Testament, after Genesis and Exodus.

indicators.note: in means the bird is tucked inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A sea-eagle is in a nervous state while building its nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'fluttER NEst'; 'building' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A white-tailed eagle of coasts, a crossword favourite for the bird.

parts.note: someone up before a judge is in court
a holder is a case or container

explanation.surface: A defence lawyer in court is carrying a briefcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: One who supports or upholds something is its defender.

parts.note: a custard is an example of a pie
eyed means looked at, regarded

explanation.surface: Someone stares at a custard while tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pie-eyed is informal for intoxicated.

clue.text: Words of reassurance from one bringing up a child?

definitions.text: Words of reassurance from one bringing up a child?

parts.words: Words of reassurance from one bringing up a child?
parts.note: 'bringing up' reads as raising a child, but it means lifting a toddler back up after a tumble, with the comforting cry said then

explanation.surface: A parent soothes the child they are raising.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation said when lifting a small child who has fallen.

clue.text: Served around Rugby as a priest

indicators.note: around means the first word's letters go on either side of the second's

parts.note: did means served, as in 'did time'
RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Someone served at Rugby School as its chaplain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugby' looks like the school or town, but here it is the sport's abbreviation; 'as a' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: A Celtic priest of ancient Britain and Gaul.

clue.text: Our bat got out modifying rhythm

indicators.note: got out suggests the letters escape their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Our batsman was dismissed, changing the tempo of the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the free stretching and shortening of tempo for expression.

parts.note: Berkshire is a breed of pig as well as an English county, so a slice of one is a cut of bacon

explanation.surface: A part of the county of Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is a county west of London, but also a black breed of pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin slice of bacon, which comes from a pig such as a Berkshire.

parts.note: edge means a lead, and at the Wimbledon tennis championships the point after deuce has a special name for that lead

explanation.surface: The outskirts of Wimbledon in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon hosts the famous tennis tournament; 'edge' is a lead, not a border.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, the point won after deuce, giving a player the upper hand.

parts.note: a plum job is a choice one
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A top-quality black pencil lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumb is the lead weight on a line used to check verticals.

parts.note: kit is an outfit of clothing or gear
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Friends bring a change of clothes to the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... to' is link wording joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Kith are one's friends and acquaintances, as in 'kith and kin'.

clue.text: There today, perhaps, from the beginning of time

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters before it might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone is there today, having been there forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges THERETODAY; 'from' is link, as in 'since ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a very long time ago, the earliest imaginable date.

clue.text: Person from one's own club, a constant friend

parts.note: stable means steady, constant
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A fellow club member is a loyal companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a horse from the same owner's yard, now any fellow member of a team or organisation.

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so these letters are re-sorted

explanation.surface: A risqué kind of seafarer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sails a pleasure boat.

indicators.note: surrounding means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: curtains is slang for the end, death

explanation.surface: Window drapes too skimpy to go round a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtains' looks like drapes but is slang for the end of life; 'of' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarcity or shortage, too little of something.

clue.text: Drink one at a time, as when winding up

parts.note: tea is a drink
singly means one at a time

explanation.surface: Drinking alone while finishing off the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding up' means teasing someone, not concluding.
explanation.definitionFit: Winding someone up is mocking them playfully, so this adverb describes that manner.

clue.text: Beetle on river, a jumper possibly

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Beetle on river, a jumper possibly' (8): WEAR is the river, but no sense of 'Beetle' gives KNIT, and a search found no source; likely an OCR misread of the clue's first word.
annotationWithheld.clue: Beetle on river, a jumper possibly

parts.note: sable is a costly fur

explanation.surface: A university's fur coat is serviceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be used is working or functional.

indicators.note: a mystery jumbles things up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A whodunnit that one listens to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hears' defines the part of the ear one hears with.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound, the organ of hearing.

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the possessive S is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: Keeping up with the style of a man named Austin.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain is to maintain or keep going.

definitions.meaning: to ... a rumour is to stamp it out

explanation.surface: Destroying someone's morale.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch is to put an end to something, and the noun is whisky from Scotland.

parts.note: a take-away counter sounds like a food shop, but it is an ancient device for counting, used for subtraction

explanation.surface: The counter of a takeaway shop open early.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient calculating frame of beads for adding and subtracting.

parts.note: a match is a marriage as well as a game, so its leading man is the one getting wed

explanation.surface: The best player in a sports game.
explanation.definitionFit: The man being married at a wedding.

clue.text: Dramatist in the same place, with old nurse

parts.note: ib. is short for ibidem, Latin for in the same place
SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse, a grade now abolished

explanation.surface: A playwright and an old nurse living together.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik, the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House.

definitions.meaning: a formal assembly or parliament in session

explanation.surface: Sitting still and not eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a legislative assembly, as in Japan, and also a controlled eating plan.

clue.text: Sink, a feature of a series of novels

parts.note: to sag is to sink or droop

explanation.surface: A kitchen sink appears in a run of novels.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long family chronicle told across several books.

clue.text: Conspirator from whom Caesar took the highest rent?

definitions.text: Conspirator from whom Caesar took the highest rent?

parts.words: Conspirator from whom Caesar took the highest rent?
parts.note: rent means a tear, not a payment: in Shakespeare this assassin struck the first blow, at Caesar's neck, from above

explanation.surface: A plotter who paid Caesar the most rent.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Roman conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Plane figure said to have destroyed approach

indicators.note: said means the phrase is spoken and heard as the answer

parts.note: wrecked means destroyed, and an angle is an approach to a problem

explanation.surface: A geometric shape reported to have spoiled a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided flat shape with right angles.

parts.note: the shafts are not ducts in a building but rays of light from the sky that warm what they hit

explanation.surface: Ducts carrying warm air.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays of sunlight that warm whatever they fall on.

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the film

parts.note: a layer is a thin film or coating

indicators.note: beginning picks the opening letter of the word it qualifies

explanation.surface: A barrister starts work in the movie business.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate is a legal professional who pleads cases.
